title: What do I know?
src: Montaigne, Essays, Apology for Raymond Sebond
idea: Montaigne took Que sais-je? as his motto. Hold your certainties loosely, because much of what we are sure of is less solid than it feels.
apply: Before arguing a point, write down what would change your mind. If nothing would, you are not reasoning yet.
who: Greg, who is certain about everything online.

msgs.x: Have you looked at the data?

scenes.nar: Greg is sure of his view, and anyone who disagrees is clueless. A stranger asks whether he has looked at the data.
When he checks, his evidence is a headline, what his friends say, and a feeling.
Montaigne's motto was, what do I know? Greg asks it, and writes down what would change his mind, and who disagrees and why.
A week later, he reads the best argument against him, and changes one position. He argues less and learns more.
